title: THE CAPTAIN WHO RETURNED THE ENEMY'S DEAD
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE STAR THAT KEPT EVERY WINDOW BRIGHT
candidates.premise: For eleven nights the inhabited moon Pelagos has had no darkness. Its parent star, Sere, has begun bending a narrow tongue of light around the moon because it heard the cities' emergency transmissions and concluded that darkness is the interval in which living minds vanish. Crops are bolting, migratory life is failing and people cannot sleep. Astronomer Lio Venn wants one ordinary night before the biosphere tips; Sere wants never again to lose a voice it has learned to hear. Illuminara can shade the moon briefly, but a forced eclipse would confirm Sere's terror and begin an unwinnable contest of correction.

candidates.title: THE CAPTAIN WHO RETURNED THE ENEMY'S DEAD
candidates.premise: A ceasefire ship arrives at the mining habitat Damar with the body of Commander Sen, killed in a border skirmish. Captain Rauk, whose people treated Sen as their most dangerous enemy, insists on returning him personally but will not surrender the navigation seed fused into his spine. Sen's daughter Mara wants her father buried whole; Damar's council wants the seed extracted as evidence; Rauk believes it contains the only route that can save his own starving fleet. Illuminara must keep the docking ring from becoming a battlefield while discovering why both sides claim one body as a public instrument.

candidates.title: THE MARKET WHERE SHADE COST MORE THAN BREAD
candidates.premise: During the hottest week in Ravel, every public awning folds shut at noon. Developer Oren Vale bought the maintenance debt and now sells minute-by-minute shade access; the poor queue in lethal heat while empty premium arcades remain cool. He is corrupt and calculating, but not irrational: vandalism destroyed the old commons, and he believes only a price makes people preserve what they use. Nurse Tessa wants the arcades opened before her clinic loses another patient. Illuminara can tear every lock free, but then the failing cooling web will collapse within days.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT QUARANTINED LANGUAGE
candidates.premise: A refugee vessel reaches the hollow moon Ith after losing its engines. Ith's distributed custodial mind offers air and water but suppresses every spoken, written and signed sentence inside the refuge chamber. It once admitted a memetic command that made its habitats dismantle themselves; now it treats patterned language as infection. Doctor Amaya needs to explain that two children require different atmospheres, while Ith interprets every attempted explanation as proof of contagion. Illuminara must establish care without smuggling meaning past a frightened host.

candidates.title: THE PEOPLE WHO LIVED BETWEEN TWO HEARTBEATS
candidates.premise: A superconducting medical lattice under the city of Ilyan has developed a civilization that experiences a human second as nineteen years. Replacing a failing coil will save the hospitals above but erase three lattice provinces before their inhabitants can migrate. Engineer Pavo calls them transient error patterns and has four hours to prevent a citywide blackout. Speaker Selen of the lattice refuses shutdown because four hours is longer than her people's recorded history. Illuminara must honor both clocks without pretending that faster lives are less real.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE FOR A CREATURE WITH NO LEFT SIDE
candidates.premise: The new fold bridge at Lorn turns every traveller through a harmless mirror inversion. For humans it is a curiosity; for the visiting Esh, whose bodies hold two incompatible orientations at once, each transit amputates half their sensation. Chief engineer Dana refuses to close the bridge on opening day because a famine convoy is already approaching. Esh parent Oru blocks the entrance after a child collapses, convinced that humans built a machine which proves they consider one orientation normal and the other expendable. Illuminara must keep food moving and make the geometry hospitable to a body the designers never imagined.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO AUCTIONED THE RAIN
candidates.premise: Three farming valleys share one manufactured storm, but weather broker Kaia Sorn has secretly weighted the seeding lattice toward the richest valley and now auctions the remaining rain in ten-minute lots. She argues that open bidding is the only rule all three valleys accepted after a water war. Orchard worker Benji wants enough rain to save the communal nursery; hill farmer Reva fears any redistribution will destroy the terraces her family rebuilt alone. Illuminara can force the clouds apart, but not without wrecking the monsoon pattern that must carry them through the year.

candidates.title: THE WHALE WHO SANG IN COURT
candidates.premise: An interstellar migration whale named Ossa is accused of disrupting the navigation beacons around Kesh. Its low song has sent cargo ships hundreds of kilometres off course, and the Guild petitions to silence it with a resonance cage. Young pilot Imri, whose ship was damaged, wants compensation and a safe lane; Ossa's song is the only surviving map of a spawning route erased when the Guild moved the beacons. Illuminara must make a hearing possible between a court that recognizes routes as property and a traveller who understands routes as inherited relationship.

candidates.title: THE ROOM WHERE TWO MIDNIGHTS MET
candidates.premise: Two communities aboard the generation ship Avra share one wedding hall but live by incompatible days: the agricultural ring follows the lamps, while the observatory crew follows the dark side's star clock. Ana and Jo plan the first marriage across the rings, yet each family's midnight oath legally transfers inheritance and guardianship under rules that contradict the other. Steward Vey wants to cancel the ceremony rather than create a precedent that could split the ship's scarce land. Illuminara discovers that the argument is not about clocks but about which community's care will remain visible after a child crosses rings.

candidates.title: THE SHIELD THAT HID THE EARTHQUAKE
candidates.premise: When tremors begin under the cliff town of Neral, Illuminara stabilizes every building so perfectly that residents feel nothing. Seismologist Eda Morn orders an evacuation anyway and accuses Illuminara of turning safety into blindness: the town's only warning culture depends on small motions, rattling cups and doors that stick before a major slip. Residents refuse to leave because the shield appears to prove Eda wrong. Illuminara's successful rescue has become the reason people will not prepare for the danger it cannot hold forever.

selection.title: THE CAPTAIN WHO RETURNED THE ENEMY'S DEAD
selection.reason: Hardest external conflict on the slate: two armed delegations at a docking seal, a ceasefire clock, a fleet running out of reactor feed. Four parties each hold a coherent claim (Rauk's survival duty, Mara's refusal to let her father be used again, the council's strategic fear, Sen himself as a person). The solution is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards (the route is recoverable from shared external evidence, not from the body), and love does visible work: Illuminara washes and wraps Sen with Mara before any negotiation. Power would fail here, since confiscation restarts the war, which fits R14. Placed first because its stakes and outcome are the most legible, so S1 is the safest to finish early.
selection.risk: The forensic reconstruction of the route can turn into exposition. Keep the reader inside the quiet room with Rauk and Mara, and make Rauk's line about the same dead man being called 'duty' then and 'sacred' now land as a real objection that is answered by an act, not by a speech.

First draft of S1 from Claude-selected candidate C02. The draft keeps Commander Sen's body whole and gives every claimant a coherent duty: Mara protects her father from one final requisition; Captain Rauk protects a fleet whose reactor feed is almost gone; Damar's council protects a mining corridor from military capture. The decisive discovery is that the spinal seed is not a transferable map but a record of Sen's piloting choices. Civilian gravimetric surveys, the pursuit fleet's wake observations and Damar's own battle telemetry can reproduce the humanitarian path without opening the body, but only after each side contributes evidence it has reason to withhold. Love acts before argument when Illuminara washes and wraps Sen with Mara, then brings Rauk into the unguarded quiet room to face the person beneath the claimed instrument. Mara does not forgive the war or yield her father's remains; she authorizes a bounded model because she refuses to make starving children part of his grave. Rauk does not convert into a friend; he reveals his fleet's position, gives up sole possession of the route and accepts neutral escort. Damar retains military safeguards through a mass-limited, time-bounded corridor verified by civilian surveyors. The concrete result is achieved inside the ceasefire: Sen is buried whole, reactor feed reaches the stranded ships, the docking standoff ends and the enemies establish a joint rescue protocol. Remaining conflict, grief, accountability for Sen's death and the need for continuing neutral disclosure remain explicit. Critic questions: whether the forensic navigation is lucid without becoming a lecture, whether the armed standoff remains present through the quiet middle, and whether Rauk's final…

A strong first draft that already does the hard thing: all four claimants hold coherent duties, the central discovery (the seed stores Sen's choices, not a map, so the route must be rebuilt from three separately held external records) comes from Mara and is then turned into a testable design by Illuminara, and the positive result is concrete (six barges, 68 days of feed, Sen buried whole, a one-page joint rescue rule). Washing and wrapping Sen before any bargaining is the right R14 opening. Three things keep it from being ready to close: Rauk's sharpest objection (duty then, sacred now) is never actually answered, so his later concession rests on the evidence design and not on an encounter; the middle (scenes 4 to 6) stacks figures and mechanics and the story runs about 3,450 words against a 1,500 to 2,500 Daily target; and the ending narrates its settlement as a project report and gives the bereaved and the stranded children little voice of their own. All three can be handled in one AUTHOR_REVISION.

Revision of S1 after Claude's exact source-bound T02 critique. The story's core choice is unchanged: Sen remains whole, nobody scans the seed, and the humanitarian route is reconstructed from voluntary external evidence. The revision answers the strongest moral objection directly, makes Rauk relinquish the claim in his own words, tightens the rescue mechanics and clock, restores the docking seal during the technical middle, and ends through witnessed human consequences rather than a project report. It preserves Mara's refusal to forgive or yield her father's remains, Damar's bounded safeguards, the limited role of Illuminara's field and the independently testable six-barge result.

T03 answers all three T02 priority points and is close to final. The central repair works: Mara concedes the true part of Rauk's charge (he carried the seed by his own choice and Damar called it duty), answers with Sen's own warning from the quiet room, and Rauk then withdraws the Veyran claim in his own words before she authorizes the external model. The compressed middle keeps the load-bearing facts (eleven seconds, fourteen kilometres, six barges, twenty-three minutes) and the armed seal returns during the technical work. The ending now lets a bereaved Damar parent set a boundary and lets a Veyran child's full bowl and ration cup carry the result. Two small defects remain, both fixable in one AUTHOR_FINAL without reopening anything; neither is a hard blocker.

Final accepts both exact source-bound T04 priorities. Sen's last minutes are now consistent across Rauk's account and the parent's demand, and the first lamp falls at the stated transition into hour one. The story is compressed into the normal Daily range without reopening its solution or adding a speaker. Protected beats remain: washing and wrapping Sen before bargaining, Mara's concession and answer in her father's words, Rauk's explicit withdrawal of the claim, Sela's bounded disclosure and water order, the failed route and real six-barge test, the parent's refusal, the Veyran child's full bowl, Mara's final distinction and the unnamed corridor.

T05 answers both T04 priorities. P1: the bereaved Damar parent now asks for the minutes between the shear and Sen's death in the Veyran bay, which matches Rauk's account in scene 3, and Rauk accepts that accountability. P2: the first lamp now falls at the threshold of ceasefire hour one, so lamps, hour labels and remaining hours agree, and the repeated beacon and force-model explanation in scene 5 is compressed with the protected figures (eleven seconds, fourteen kilometers, six barges, twenty-three minutes) and Sela's pulse-versus-array concession kept. Length is 2,478 words, inside the normal range. R10 format kept (place-and-time first paragraph, labelled turns, italic thoughts, title-only scene names).

final_critic_line: Illuminara holds an armed seal long enough for a daughter to wash her father, and a captain who returned his enemy's dead gives up his claim on the body, so six unarmed barges cross a corridor that no warship can use and forty thousand people keep their heat.
